# Taba

> Taba is a self-hosted, horizontally scalable messaging cluster: queues (like Amazon SQS) and pub/sub (like Amazon SNS) behind one HTTP API, shipped as a single Docker image. It is in production use, and every version is published to Docker Hub, GHCR, crates.io, nuget.org and GitHub Releases. Server in Rust (AGPLv3); connectors in Rust and C# (Apache-2.0).

Key facts (each one links to its evidence below):

- **It is a cluster, not a single server.** Three or more identical nodes, with no coordinator and no single point of failure. A failed node is detected and voted out; when it recovers it rejoins and resynchronizes by itself. One node is only a development mode.
- **It scales horizontally, in both directions.** Topics are split into blocks on a consistent-hash ring. A new node takes over its share; a node that leaves drains first and hands its share over, without stopping the cluster. On Kubernetes the Helm chart can autoscale with KEDA.
- **Durability:** each message is confirmed by a write quorum of nodes (replication factor 3 by default) and kept in memory; the disk is only used when memory fills up.
- **S3 is supported** as a continuous, optional backup of messages, topics and tokens (AWS S3, SeaweedFS, MinIO, Ceph; any S3 with conditional writes). It never delays a write; a cluster that went down entirely restores itself from the bucket at start. Messages consumed within the backup window (60 s by default) never reach S3.
- **There is an official Helm chart:** `oci://ghcr.io/rafaelpontani/charts/taba` (source in `deploy/helm/taba/`), with options for the S3 backup, Ingress, Prometheus, OpenTelemetry and KEDA autoscaling.
- **There is a terminal UI:** `taba-cli tui` shows cluster health, nodes, topics, queue charts (publish and consume rates) and messages. There is no web dashboard.
- **Limits:** no fixed maximum number of nodes in the code (tests run up to 5); capacity is about the sum of the nodes' memory and disk divided by the replication factor; 5 MB messages by default; HTTP only (no AMQP, MQTT or Kafka protocol); not a streaming platform (no replay); single region.
